subject: brain
topic: The brain can physically rewire itself to become more prone to addiction
angle: Substance use disorders involve maladaptive neuroplasticity and neuroinflammation that alter reward and decision-making circuitry, creating persistent vulnerabilities like cue-induced seeking.
title: The Physicality of Addiction

hooks.text: Is your craving a choice or a physical rewiring?
You think you are choosing the substance. Your brain has already rewired the choice.
Your habits are physically altering your decision-making circuitry.
A familiar street corner and a sudden, physical pull.
Substance use causes structural changes in the brain.

reveal.headline: Your brain physically rewires itself to favor addiction.
reveal.body: Chronic substance use creates maladaptive neuroplasticity and brain inflammation that alter your reward and decision-making circuitry.

explain.headline: Inflammation changes your neural pathways.
explain.body: Drug exposure triggers gliosis and cytokine release. This inflammation, combined with oxidative stress, alters the systems that govern your motivation and how you make choices.

matters.headline: Your environment becomes a trigger.
matters.body: The brain develops persistent vulnerabilities like cue-induced seeking. That may be why certain places or objects can trigger a craving even after long periods of abstinence.

example.headline: A specific street corner at night.
example.body: You walk past a familiar building. A specific smell or sight triggers a physical urge to seek a substance, even though you haven't used in months.

question.headline: Which parts of your routine are actually physical triggers?

stat.label: the structural and functional changes in the brain's reward systems

claims.text: Lifestyle medicine may help strengthen substance use recovery through healthy neuroplastic changes.
claims.quote: lifestyle medicine offers a valuable adjunct therapy that may help strengthen substance use recovery through healthy neuroplastic changes.

claims.text: A specific type of receptor (CP-AMPARs) in the nucleus accumbens is linked to cue-induced seeking that persists even after long periods of abstinence.
claims.quote: In particular, an atypical subpopulation-Ca2+-permeable or CP-AMPARs-mediates cue-induced seeking that persists even after long periods of abstinence

claims.text: Chronic exposure to addictive drugs is linked to brain inflammation characterized by gliosis, microglial activation, and sustained release of cytokines.
claims.quote: Chronic exposure to addictive drugs in substance use disorders and stressors in mood disorders render the brain more vulnerable to inflammation. Inflammation in the brain, or neuroinflammation, is characterized by gliosis, microglial activation, and sustained release of cytokines

claims.text: Neuroinflammation and oxidative stress are linked to altering neural circuitry involved in reward, motivation, negative affect, and decision-making.
claims.quote: Recent studies emphasize the critical roles of neuroinflammation and oxidative stress in shaping SUDs by altering neural circuitry involved in reward, motivation, negative affect, and decision-making

claims.text: Substance use disorder is linked to the consolidation of maladaptive neuroplasticity affecting dopaminergic, glutamatergic, and neurotrophic systems.
claims.quote: Substance use disorder (SUD) is a complex neurobiological disorder characterized by the consolidation of maladaptive neuroplasticity affecting dopaminergic, glutamatergic, and neurotrophic systems

claims.text: Cocaine-induced plasticity in the nucleus accumbens is linked to cocaine seeking.
claims.quote: We have learned the most about cocaine-induced plasticity in the nucleus accumbens and its relationship to cocaine seeking

verdict: The evidence shows that substance use causes structural and functional changes in the brain's reward and executive systems through maladaptive neuroplasticity and inflammation.
caveat: There is a scarcity of longitudinal studies and limited clinical generalizability across the current research.
caption:
Your brain can physically change its structure in response to substance use.

Research shows that chronic exposure leads to neuroinflammation and maladaptive neuroplasticity in reward and executive systems. There is currently a scarcity of longitudinal studies and limited clinical generalizability.

How does your environment influence your cravings?
